title: Ears and tails · the shape-shifters
blurb: The breeds defined by one changed part: a folded ear, a curled ear, no tail or very short legs, each fixed by a single gene.

items.d: The tailless cat of the Isle of Man, with a rounded rump and a hopping gait.
Japan's short-tailed cat, with a pom-pom tail and a place in the maneki-neko figure.
A short-tailed cat found in Arizona in the 1960s, with a wild, hunting look.
A Russian island cat with a short, kinked tail and a thick double coat.
A breed from California, 1981, defined by ears that curl back instead of standing up.
The folded-ear cat of Scotland, 1961, with a round head and an owl-like look.
The short-legged cat of the 1980s, with normal-sized body and a low-slung walk.
Thailand's white cat of the royal court, with jewel-coloured eyes and a short coat.
